subject: BrightRetail pilot: TTFT targets & streaming roadmap
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sam Garcia <sam.garcia@brightretail.com>, Priya Singh <priya.s@brightretail.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: BrightRetail pilot: TTFT targets & streaming roadmap

Hi Sam / Priya —

Great conversation earlier — thanks for walking us through the BrightRetail realtime search use case. Posting a short recap and the asks we agreed on so we have a clear pilot plan.

Key performance targets you mentioned
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): P50 target <= 250ms, P95 goal <= 600ms for 1k QPS search fan-out (initial).
- Steady-state throughput: target 600–1,000 qps across the cluster during peak hour (read-heavy).
- Concurrency: expect bursts up to ~1,200 concurrent in-flight streaming responses during flash sales.
- Streaming mode: you prefer server-sent events (SSE) based on client constraints; WebSocket is possible but some edge proxies drop WS frequently.
- Chunk cadence: you asked for the first meaningful chunk as small/fast as possible (ideally within 150–300ms), subsequent chunks ok at 50–120ms intervals for steady generation.

Open technical questions for the pilot
1) Can BrightRetail accept SSE-only for the first phase, or do you need dual-mode (SSE + WS) from day one?
2) Do you have strict connection limits per origin (e.g., max concurrent connections per client IP) from your CDN/edge?
3) Can you share a small sample of typical payload sizes and prompt lengths (tokens)? even a 50–100 example sample will help sizing.

Next steps (proposal)
- Redwood will stand up a 2-week pilot: dedicated capacity with a 3-node serving pool tuned for streaming.
- Run a short probe (3–6 hours) using streaming_probe_config.yaml (attached) to measure TTFT, chunk cadence, and tail at target QPS.
- Success criteria: TTFT P50 <= 250ms and P95 <= 600ms while maintaining requested concurrency with acceptable quality.

Attachments: pilot_scope_v1.pdf (high-level SOW), streaming_probe_config.yaml (probe plan), redwood_streaming_card.png (diagram).

If that summary looks right I’ll book a short kickoff this week and loop in Aditya/Karthik for the probe.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Sam Garcia <sam.garcia@brightretail.com>

Cc: Priya Singh <priya.s@brightretail.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightRetail pilot: TTFT targets & streaming roadmap

Tessa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick clarifications from our side:
- SSE is preferred for phase 1. Our edge (FastEdge CDN) occasionally terminates long-lived WS connections for mobile chrome views; SSE has been much more stable in our experience.
- Concurrent connections per client: we throttle to ~200 connections/IP (we're ok with multiple IPs during the pilot).
- Prompt sizes: typical search prompt ~40–120 tokens, average completion length ~80 tokens. Payloads mostly short text snippets, some JSON-wrapped metadata.

A couple of asks:
1) If we hit capacity limits, can Redwood automatically fall back to a lower-cost but lower-throughput model (smaller parameter variant) to avoid request failures?
2) What visibility will we get into per-token latency (P50/P95) and chunk cadence during the probe — can those be exported to our monitoring (Prometheus)?

We should be conservative with concurrency at first — start with 30–40 concurrent streams per region and ramp. Also cost will be a gating factor: can you share an expected per-1kQPS cost estimate for the pilot config in the SOW?

Happy to run the probe later this week — I’ll let Priya confirm availability.

—Sam
Head of Search Infrastructure, BrightRetail
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightRetail pilot: TTFT targets & streaming roadmap

Tessa / Karthik —

Looping in a short technical note to address Sam’s asks and propose concrete probe parameters.

Short answers to Sam’s questions:
- Graceful fallback: yes — our routing supports automatic fallback to a smaller model variant (same tokenizer) when the primary tier is saturated. Fallback is policy-driven and can be configured to prefer latency or cost.
- Visibility: we expose per-request/tokens latency metrics, chunk emit timestamps, and per-route P50/P95/P99 via the Console API. We can stream a subset of metrics to your Prometheus via our remote_write integration for the pilot.

Probe suggestions (config attached: streaming_probe_config.yaml)
- Model & profile: start with open-llm-medium variant (balanced) with fallback to open-llm-small for overload.
- Node pool & concurrency: 3 dedicated GPUs, target steady concurrency 30 per node (90 total); can burst to 120 total for short windows with autoscaling buffer. This aligns with your conservative ramp ask.
- Batching & kernels: continuous batching with small batch timeout (8–12ms) to preserve TTFT for short prompts; choose kernels optimized for streaming (KV cache warm start).
- Chunk cadence targets: first chunk target 120–220ms (includes network + model start); subsequent chunk cadence target 60–110ms. We’ll instrument emitted chunk timestamps to verify.
- Ramp plan: start at 30 concurrency for 1 hour, validate TTFT and P95. If stable, move to 60 for 2 hours, then 90 for a 3–4 hour soak.

Data we need from BrightRetail for probe accuracy:
- 200 representative prompts (anonymized) and a distribution of expected completion lengths.
- Any IP-based connection limits at CDN or LB to configure client pooling.

Risk & mitigations:
- If WS termination is observed at scale, we'll enforce SSE at the edge and optionally multiplex multiple SSE streams per connection via a lightweight stub on the app layer.
- If P95 exceeds 600ms at 90 concurrency, policy will trigger rollback to smaller model and an alert to both teams.

I’ve attached the probe YAML and a short diagram. I’ll be available for the kickoff and can run the probe with BrightRetail credentials once we have sample prompts.

-Aditya
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sam / Priya —

Perfect — thanks for the quick clarifications. Action items & mutual action plan below so we’re aligned:

BrightRetail (you):
- Share 200 anonymized prompts + token distribution (upload to the secure Drive link Sam will send).
- Confirm SSE-only for phase 1 (reply to this thread).
- Confirm calendar slots for kickoff (I shared a link: https://cal.com/tessa/30).

Redwood (we):
- Provision 3-node dedicated serving pool and upload probe config (we’ll run the streaming_probe_config.yaml in the attached SOW).
- Run the probe: 1 hour @30 concurrency -> 2 hours @60 -> 3 hours @90, capture P50/P95/P99 for TTFT and per-chunk timestamps.
- Provide Prometheus remote_write endpoint + Grafana dashboard link for real-time visibility.
- If P95 > 600ms at 90 concurrency we will auto-fallback to open-llm-small and surface results to BrightRetail.

Success criteria for the pilot (agreeable to both sides):
- TTFT: P50 <= 250ms, P95 <= 600ms during target concurrency windows.
- Chunk cadence: first chunk median <= 220ms; subsequent chunks median <= 110ms.
- No >1% error rate for streaming emits across the soak window.

Deliverables: pilot report (latency histograms, chunk timeline traces), recommended production config, and a draft order form with estimated pilot cost.

I’ll schedule kickoff once Priya confirms the prompt upload and a time. If you confirm SSE-only and the sample upload by EOD tomorrow we can run the probe by Friday.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
